text:
alex: quick check-in — saw a couple of 99.9th token latency spikes in prod when tenant 'atlas' bursts (~1k r/s). hypothesis: our continuous batcher is filling, then suddenly evicting/reshaping batches which causes long tail. proposing a 'soft-spill' policy: per-tenant spill buffer that absorbs overflow without immediate eviction, uses probabilistic admission and deadline tags. thoughts?

nina: can you paste a short trace? curious where the time is spent (enqueue vs kernel).

alex: paste from span (trimmed):
```
enqueue: 3ms
coalesce: 18ms
batch_wait: 240ms  <-- long
gpu_dispatch: 5ms
kernel_time: 24ms
```
The batch_wait jump correlates with a refactor we merged that aggressively compacts windows.

omar: so compaction is best-effort, right? if compaction runs while new small requests keep arriving, we might keep postponing dispatch until a compaction epoch finishes.

liam: yeah and compaction does a global shrink that can trigger reallocation/evictions of queued items. That can push some requests to fallback slowpath.

sara: soft-spill sounds promising. A few clarifying constraints:
- mustn't increase p50
- limited memory for extra buffers (we have ~64MB per-GPU spare)
- metrics must show per-tenant spill rate and how often spilled items actually rejoin fastpath

alex: agreed. Implementation sketch:
1) admission to main coalesce queue remains unchanged until occupancy > soft_threshold (e.g., 75% of target batch size distribution).
2) overflow requests are placed in per-tenant spill queue (ring buffer) with small TTL (e.g., 50ms).
3) spill queue uses probabilistic admission when near capacity: new admitted with prob p = max(0.1, 1 - occupancy).
4) when a main batch is about to dispatch, it pulls a bounded number from spill queues respecting deadlines.
5) if TTL expires, promote to slowpath (dedicated tiny-batch path) rather than drop.

Code sketch (pseudocode):
```
if main_queue.len() >= soft_limit:
  if tenant_spill.len() < spill_cap && rand() < admit_prob(tenant_spill):
    tenant_spill.push(req)
  else:
    route_to_slowpath(req)
else:
  main_queue.push(req)
```

omar: couple tradeoffs:
- extra copying/queue hops = CPU overhead per-request
- we might end up with tenant starvation if we always prefer main queue fill from big tenants' spill buffers

liam: add per-tenant fairness tokens: each dispatch cycle can pull at most N tokens per tenant unless main_queue underutilized. that prevents a noisy neighbor from monopolizing spill drain.

nina: how do we handle kv-cache pinning? evicting from main queue currently triggers KV cache rewrites for some requests. If we spill instead of evicting, we avoid some eviction churn (win). but if TTLed requests go to slowpath we still incur work. need to measure.

alex: good point. we should tag spilled items with their KV fingerprints so slowpath can skip reloading if a subsequent promoted request still has KV present. add a "kv_tag" on the spill entry.

sara: observability: needed metrics
- spill_enqueue_count{tenant}
- spill_drain_count{tenant}
- spill_ttl_expire_count{tenant}
- avg_spill_hold_ms{tenant}
- p99_batch_wait_with_spill
- slowpath_promote_rate{tenant}
and traces to cover a request occasionally hitting each state.

omar: I ran a microbench on branch with a naive spill (no fairness, 30ms TTL) against a synthetic burst. results (50k requests):
- baseline 99.9th: 620ms
- naive-spill 99.9th: 210ms
- p50/p90 almost identical
- CPU user increased ~7%
So big win for tail with small CPU cost.

liam: that's excellent. did you test with multiple tenants bursting? noisy-neighbor scenario?

omar: with two equal noisy tenants both bursting, naive-spill improved tails for both but one tenant could sometimes starve the other due to drain ordering.

alex: so we need the fairness token limiter from liam and smarter drain ordering (deadline-aware). proposal: drain prioritizes entries with the earliest application-level deadline tag, fallback to fairness round-robin if deadlines similar.

nina: deadlines are tricky — callers don't always set them. we can synthesize soft-deadlines based on request size and RTT budget heuristics. add a flag to allow callers to pass explicit deadline header for critical requests.

sara: config knobs we need in console: soft_limit_pct, spill_ttl_ms, spill_cap_per_tenant, fairness_tokens_per_dispatch, synth_deadline_frac, admit_prob_floor. Also expose a per-tenant override for enterprise customers.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: feature-flag behind runtime.soft_spill; canary to 10% of hosts; telemetry hook required (see observability list).

alex: next steps:
- Omar to harden spill queues with fairness tokens + deadline ordering (PR)
- Nina to add KV-tag plumbing to spill entries + tracing points
- Sara to spec metrics + console knobs (PR)
- Liam to run multi-tenant stress tests and gather cost impact
- I'll draft an RFC addendum summarizing algorithm and config surface

sara: timeline?

omar: aim for a small experimental rollout in 2 weeks. canary 1; measure p99 and CPU overhead.

liam: fine with that. I'll set up the harness.

alex: thanks — good progress. @sara can you add the metrics to the telemetry board and create the console feature flag entry? :thumbsup:
